extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational-linguistics researchers and practitioners working on sarcasm detection, humor classification, and code-mixed (Hindi-English) multimodal conversational datasets and models
extracted.subtask_short: sarcasm and humor detection in code-mixed dialogs
extracted.subtask_description: Designing datasets and models for multi-modal sarcasm detection and humor classification in Hindi-English code-mixed conversational utterances, including architecture choices (attention mechanisms), multimodal feature usage, evaluation, and analysis. Focuses on dataset creation, model design (hierarchical and dialog-level attention), experiments across modal inputs, and diagnostic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contextual and non-verbal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Sarcasm detection and humor classification are inherently subtle problems, primarily due to their dependence on the contextual and non-verbal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models and datasets should capture conversational context (dialog history) and non-verbal cues (multimodal signals) because these signals are crucial to disambiguate sarcasm and humor from literal utterances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code-mixed, multi-modal conversational dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a Hindi-English code-mixed dataset, MaSaC, for the multi-modal sarcasm detection and humor classification in conversational dialog (first dataset of its kind per the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset should be code-mixed (Hindi-English), include multi-modal inputs (text + non-verbal modalities), be conversational (utterance-level within dialog), and be qualitatively annotated for sarcasm and humor to support training and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical attention for utterance representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn efficient utterance representation utilizing a hierarchical attention mechanism that attends to a small portion of the input sentence at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectures should include hierarchical attention that focuses on salient subparts of an utterance to build stronger representations for classification; design choices and justification for this mechanism should be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialog-level contextual attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate dialog-level contextual attention mechanism to leverage the dialog history for the multi-modal classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models must explicitly model and attend over dialog history/context (not only isolated utterances) to improve sarcasm/humor detection in conversational settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multi-modal inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform multi-modal classification by varying multi-modal inputs and evaluating their contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments should include combinations of modalities (e.g., text plus non-verbal signals) to show how each modality contributes; reporting modality-specific ablations is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation and submodule analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform experiments by varying various submodules of the proposed architecture (MSH-COMICS) to understand contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct systematic ablation studies that remove or alter components (e.g., hierarchical attention, dialog-level attention) to quantify their impact on performance and justify architectural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evaluation against existing approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct comparative analysis against existing approaches to demonstrate relative performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare proposed models and dataset results with prior state-of-the-art and baseline models using the same metrics and data splits to substantiate claims of improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate evaluation metrics (F1-score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report performance using metrics such as F1-score (paper reports improvements: >1 F1 point for sarcasm detection and 10 F1 points in humor classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard classification metrics (particularly F1 for imbalanced labels) and report absolute scores and differences versus baselines; clearly state evaluation protocol and splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model diagnosis and error analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnose the model and perform thorough analysis of the results to understand the superiority and pitfalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include qualitative and quantitative error analysis to reveal strengths, failure modes, and limitations of the model; discuss when and why the model succeeds or fails (e.g., types of sarcasm/humor it misses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address scarcity of annotated code-mixed resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize existing studies are constrained in non-English languages such as Hindi due to the unavailability of qualitative annotated datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working on code-mixed languages, explicitly address dataset availability and annotation quality (e.g., annotation guidelines, inter-annotator agreement) and provide resources to mitigate low-resource challenges.
